Penalized quasi-likelihood for generalized linear mixed models

Source: R/pql.R
pql_regcomp.Rd

Fits a GLMM by penalized quasi-likelihood (Breslow and Clayton 1993): repeated linear mixed model fits, by maximum likelihood, to the working response z = eta + (y - mu) deta/dmu with variance weights (dmu/deta)^2 / V(mu), as MASS::glmmPQL(). PQL is not a likelihood method (no log likelihood, AIC or likelihood ratio tests); it is biased for binary data with few observations per cluster, where the Laplace fit of regcomp() is preferable. It handles quasi families.

Usage

pql_regcomp(formula, family, data, niter = 10, tol = 1e-06)

Arguments

formula

A formula with lme4 style random effects, y ~ x + (1 | g).

family

A stats::family() object (such as binomial(), poisson(), quasipoisson()).

data

A data frame.

niter

Maximum number of iterations.

tol

Convergence tolerance on the linear predictor.

Value

The final working normal mixed model fit (a regcomp_fit), whose mu coefficients are the fixed effects on the link scale and whose theta are the random effect parameters, with class regcomp_pql added and the number of iterations in iterations.

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(g = factor(rep(1:20, each = 8)), x = rnorm(160))
d$y <- rpois(160, exp(0.3 + 0.4 * d$x + rnorm(20, 0, 0.5)[d$g]))
pql_regcomp(y ~ x + (1 | g), family = poisson(), data = d)
#> <regcomp_pql> poisson (log link) GLMM by penalized quasi-likelihood, 5 iterations, n = 160
#>             estimate std_error      z
#> (Intercept)   0.5573    0.1309 4.2560
#> x             0.3785    0.0616 6.1499
#> Random effect parameters:
#> mu:1 | g:log_sd((Intercept)) 
#>                      -0.6645
